MIZORAM PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
COMPETITIVE EXAMINATION FOR INSPECTOR OF STATISTICS
 UNDER PLANNING & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION DEPARTMENT,
GOVERNMENT OF MIZORAM.
(MARCH-2026)
PAPER-I
(GENERAL ENGLISH)
Time Allowed : 3 hours
FM : 150
Mark for each question is indicated against it.
1. Write an essay choosing one of the topics given below:
(20)
(a) Sairang Rail Station: A Catalyst for Infrastructure Development in Mizoram
(b) Mental Health and Work Environment
(c) Strengthening Good Governance through Official Statistics
(d) The Digital Generation: How Technology is Changing Childhood and Youth.
2. Write a precis of the following passage:
(10)
Self-reliance is the pilgrim’s best staff, the worker’s best tool. It is the master key that
unlocks all the difficulties of life. ‘Help yourself and Heaven will help you’ is a maxim that receives
daily confirmation. He who begins with crutches will generally end with crutches. Help from within
always strengthens, but help from without invariably weakens the recipients. The habit of depending
upon others should be vigorously resisted, since it tends to weaken the intellectual faculties and
paralyse the judgement. The struggle against adverse circumstances has, on the contrary, a strengthening
effect, like that of the pure mountain air on an enfeebled frame.
This is a lesson which is not taught in academic institutions nowadays. The vice of the
modern system of education is that it lays down too many royal roads to knowledge. The difficulties,
which formerly compelled the student to think and labour for himself are now mire carefully removed.
The race of thorough and complete scholars is dying out. Our young men are equipped to such an
extent with manuals that explain everything and guides that go everywhere, that they find no occasion
for thought. Why take any trouble at all when so many are willing to relieve you of it?

- 2 -
Direction (Question Nos. 3 -12): Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the
given passage.
Many people believe that science and religion are contrary to each other. But this notation
is wrong. As a matter of fact, both are correlated to each other. There is no doubt that the method of
science and religion are different. The method of science is observation, experimentation and
experience. Science takes its recourse to progressive march towards perfection. The rules of religion
are faith, intuition and spoken word of the enlightened. In general, while science is inclined towards
reason and rationality, spiritualism is the essence of religion.
In earlier times when man appeared on Earth, he was over-awed at the sight of violent and
powerful aspects of nature. In certain cases, the usefulness of different natural objects of nature
overwhelmed man. Thus began the worship of forces of nature — fire, the sun, the rivers, the rocks,
the trees, the snakes etc. The holy scriptures were written by those who had developed harmony
between external nature and their inner self. Their objective was to ennoble, elevate and liberate the
human spirit and mind. But the priestly class took upon itself the monopoly of scriptural knowledge
and interpretation to its own advantage. Thus, the entire human race was in chains. Truth was flouted
and progressive, liberal and truthful ideas or ideas expressing doubt and scepticism were suppressed
and their holders punished. It was in these trying circumstances that science emerged as a saviour of
mankind. But its path was not smooth and safe. The scientists and free thinkers were tortured. This
was the fate of Copernicus, Galileo, Bruno and others. But side by side science gained ground.
3. Why does man worship the force of nature?
(2)
4. Why is it said in the passage that ‘science emerged as a saviour of mankind’?
(2)
5. According to the passage, science and religion both:
(2)
(a) Emerged out of the fear of man
(b) Emerged from the desire of man to worship the forces of nature
(c) Employs different methods of inquiry
(d) Work at the cross-purpose of each other
6. According to the passage, at the present juncture, there is a need to:
(2)
(a) teach people to worship the forces of nature
(b) encourage spiritualism as much as possible
(c) judiciously mix the principles of science and true spirit of religion
(d) free man from all sorts of bondages
7. Choose the antonym of the word ‘non-contradictory’
(2)
8. Which of the following statements is true in the context of the passage?
(2)
(a) Science and religion are antagonistic to each other
(b) Science encourages worshipping of nature
(c) Religion is essential for external peace and harmony
(d) Regimental religion was replaced by scientific principles
9. Which of the following statements is not true in the context of the passage?
(2)
(a) Man worships the forces of nature
(b) Methods of science and religion are different
(c) Regimental religion got degenerated into orthodoxy
(d) Galileo and Bruno were disciples of Copernicus

MIZORAM PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
COMPETITIVE EXAMINATION FOR RECRUITMENT TO THE POST OF
INSTRUCTOR, ITI UNDER LABOUR, EMPLOYMENT, SKILL DEVELOPMENT
& ENTREPRENEURSHIP DEPARTMENT, GOVERNMENT OF MIZORAM.
(APRIL-2026)
PAPER-I
(GENERAL ENGLISH)
Time Allowed : 3 hours
FM : 100
PART- A
(40 Marks)
This Section should be answered only on the Answer Sheet provided.
Marks for each question is indicated against it. Attempt all questions.
1. Write a precis of the following passage in about one third of the original length and suggest a suitable
title.
(10)
Skill-based training today is no longer what it used to be. With rapid technological progress
and changing industry requirements, older methods of teaching—mainly based on memorization and
repetition—have become insufficient. Workers in modern industries are expected not only to possess
technical knowledge but also to demonstrate adaptability, problem-solving ability, and readiness to
work with new technologies.
At this point, the role of instructors in Industrial Training Institutes becomes especially important.
Their responsibility goes beyond delivering lessons; they are expected to connect theoretical learning
with practical application. By guiding trainees to think independently and solve real-life problems,
instructors help them become more confident and capable. This also means that instructors themselves
must regularly upgrade their skills and remain aware of current industrial practices.
The introduction of digital tools and simulation methods has improved the training process. Yet,
these tools alone cannot guarantee effective learning. If not guided properly, trainees may perform
tasks without understanding the basic concepts behind them. Therefore, it is necessary to maintain a
balance between hands-on practice and conceptual clarity.
In the end, the goal of industrial training is to develop workers who are skilled, confident, and
adaptable. This goal can be achieved only when instructors take on the role of mentors who encourage
continuous learning.
2. Many students avoid vocational training and choose general academic courses without a proper
career plan. Write a letter to the Editor of the daily newspaper Zawlkhawpui discussing this issue and
suggesting ways to increase awareness of skilled jobs.Address yourself as XXX.
(10)

- 2 -
3. Read the following passage carefully and answer the following questions:
Industrial training plays an important role in preparing young people for employment. It focuses
on developing practical skills that are directly useful in the workplace. However, many trainees do
not fully benefit from such training because they lack seriousness and discipline. Some attend classes
irregularly, while others do not pay attention during practical sessions. Instructors try to guide trainees
by demonstrating correct methods and encouraging them to practice regularly. Still, without interest
and effort from the trainees, learning remains incomplete. In addition, the proper use of tools and
safety measures is often ignored, which can lead to accidents.
To make training effective, both instructors and trainees must work together. Trainees should
take responsibility for their learning, while instructors should create an engaging and supportive
environment. Only then can industrial training achieve its goal of producing skilled and confident
workers.
(i) What is the main purpose of industrial training?
(2)
(ii) Why do some trainees fail to benefit fully from training?
(2)
(iii) What role do instructors play in the training process?
(2)
(iv) How can industrial training be made more effective?
(2)
(v) Find a word from the passage similar in meaning to “self-control.”
(1)
(vi) Find a word from the passage opposite in meaning to “comprehensive.”
(1)
4. Write an essay on any one (1) of the following topics in about 250 words:
(10)
- The Importance of discipline in building a successful skilled career.
- Intermarriage and Mizo Women’s Rights
- Role of Information Technology in Skill Development.

- 3 -
PART- B
(60 Marks)
All questions carry equal mark of 2. Attempt all questions.
This Section should be answered only on the OMR Response Sheet provided.
Notes regarding Negative Marking :
(i) There will be penalty (negative marking) for every wrong answer given by a candidate in the
MCQ type questions.
(ii) For each question for which a wrong answer has been given by the candidate, one third of the
marks assigned to that question will be deducted as penalty.
(iii) If a candidate gives more than one answer to one question, it will be treated as wrong answer
even if one of the given answers happens to be correct and there will be same penalty as
above for that question.
(iv) If any questions is left blank i.e. no answer is given by the candidate, there will be no penalty
for that question
Direction (Question Nos 1 - 5) : Choose the correct parts of speech.

(a) Adverb
(b) Adjective
(c) Noun
(d) Pronoun
2. She has been working since morning.
(a) Conjunction
(b) Preposition
(c) Adverb
(d) Pronoun
3. She might refuse the offer without explanation.
(a) Noun
(b) Verb
(c) Adverb
(d) Pronoun
4. Nobody understood the complexity of the matter.
(a) Pronoun
(b) Noun
(c) Verb
(d) Adjective
5. His unexpected arrival caused upheaval.
(a) Verb
(b) Adjective
(c) Adverb
(d) Noun
Directions (Question Nos. 6 - 10) : Rewrite the sentences by substituting the underlined word(s) with
the appropriate parts of speech given in brackets.
6. He fought bravely during the battle. (Noun)
(a) He braved the battle.
(b) He was very brave during the battle.
(c) He fought with bravery during the battle.
(d) He fought during the battle with braveness.

- 4 -
7. We woke up to a beautiful sunrise. (Adverb)
(a) We woke up to a beautifully sunrise.
(b) We woke up to the beauty of the sunrise.
(c) We woke up to a beauteous sunrise.
(d) We woke up as the sun rose beautifully.
8. If what you have told me is true, then I must act. (Noun)
(a) If what you have told me is truly, then I must act.
(b) If what you have told me is a truism, then I must act.
(c) If what you have told me is truthful, then I must act.
(d) If what you have told me is the truth, then I must act.
9. There was a gentle breeze that blew in from the east. (Adverb)
(a) The breeze blew in from the east with gentleness.
(b) The breeze blew in from the east with gentility.
(c) The breeze blew in from the east genteelly.
(d) The wind blew in gently from the east.
10. I am happy to be in the king’s service .(Verb)
(a) I am happy to serve the king.
(b) I am happy to be serviceable to the king.
(c) I am happy with my servitude to the king.
(d) I am happy to be in the king’s servitude.
Directions (Question No. 11 - 15) : Identify the correct meaning of the following idioms and phrases.

12. to be under the weather

13. To break the ice

(b) to start a new venture or journey with limited resources
(c) to accidentally ruin a situation which was already delicate to start with
(d) to say or do something to make people comfortable in a social setting
14. to let the cat out of the bag
(a) to free someone from a debt or an obligation
(b) to accidentally reveal a secret
(c) to solve a problem easily
(d) to conclude something in a favourable manner

(b) you are more fortunate than you think
(c) it is your turn to act or make a decision
